title: Summary statistic for pulsar timing arrays
comment: 18 pages, 9 figures
summary: The timing residuals produced by gravitational-wave signals can be described as an incoherent (pulsar term) contribution and a coherent (Earth term) map on the sky, which PTAs measure at the locations of the timed pulsars. The observed Earth term map and the variance induced by the pulsar term contain all of the information about any GW signal available to a PTA (assuming pulsar distances are unknown). Furthermore, any type of signal produces on average the same angular correlation function, the Hellings and Downs curve, which decays steeply with multipole as $C_\ell \propto 1/[(\ell+2)(\ell+1)\ell(\ell-1)]$. This suggests that the signal is inherently low-dimensional and therefore only a small number of parameters are needed to fully characterize it. We present an expression for the PTA likelihood that makes the dependence on the Earth term map and pulsar term variance explicit, and show that only a few spherical harmonic coefficients are needed to capture most of the information about the signal. To quantify this in a realistic setting, we compute the Fisher matrix of the amplitude of a stochastic background or a deterministic point source assuming the noise properties and sky locations of the pulsars in the NANOGrav 15yr dataset. We find that $\ell_{\rm max}=2$ of the Earth term map and the monopole of the pulsar term variance retain $\sim 95\%$ of the information about the signal. For a point source, including the dipole of the pulsar term variance is important to achieve a similar fraction.

AI.tldr: The paper shows that PTA gravitational-wave signals are inherently low-dimensional: the Earth-term sky map and pulsar-term variance fully capture all information about any GW signal. Using the NANOGrav 15yr dataset, they demonstrate via Fisher matrix analysis that only a few spherical harmonic coefficients (ℓ_max=2 for the Earth term and monopole of the pulsar term) retain ~95% of the signal information, with the dipole of the pulsar term becoming important for point sources.
AI.motivation: To determine the minimal number of parameters needed to fully characterize gravitational-wave signals in pulsar timing arrays, given that all GW signals produce the same Hellings and Downs angular correlation function which decays steeply with multipole, suggesting a low-dimensional signal structure.
AI.method: The authors present an expression for the PTA likelihood that makes the dependence on the Earth term map and pulsar term variance explicit. They then compute the Fisher matrix of the amplitude for both a stochastic background and a deterministic point source, using the noise properties and sky locations of pulsars in the NANOGrav 15yr dataset.
AI.result: They find that ℓ_max=2 of the Earth term map plus the monopole of the pulsar term variance retain ~95% of the information about the signal. For a point source, additionally including the dipole of the pulsar term variance is needed to achieve a similar information fraction.
AI.conclusion: PTA gravitational-wave signals are inherently low-dimensional and can be efficiently parameterized with only a small number of spherical harmonic coefficients, enabling more compact and computationally efficient analyses of PTA data.

title: 3-form dark energy and cosmic birefringence
comment: 15 pages, 3 figures
summary: 3-forms are interesting fields to study in the cosmological context for numerous reasons, such as being candidates for explaining inflation and dark energy. The background evolution of a 3-form field is similar to but distinguishable from a scalar field in an expanding universe, and its tensorial structure allows for unique couplings that cannot be experienced by canonical scalars. In this work, we explore the possibility that 3-form dark energy can explain cosmic birefringence. We consider two EFT-inspired couplings between the 3-form and the photon, and compute the birefringence angle $β$. We find that a dimension-6 gauge-invariant operator necessitates an extremely large coupling to explain $β\sim0.3^\circ$, the value suggested by observations of recent cosmic microwave background radiation. Conversely, a dimension-4 operator can accommodate $β\sim0.3^\circ$ at the expense exciting the longitudinal mode of the photon. Interestingly, demanding a self-consistent decoupling limit implies the photon mass lies within a few orders of magnitude of $H_0$. We also derive `universal' profiles for $β(z)$, finding the $β$ from the dimension-4 operator is insensitive to the form of the 3-form potential but is sensitive to the initial conditions. Contrarily, the dimension-6 operator is highly sensitive to the form of the potential. We finally compare the universal profiles to that of axion-like particle (ALP) dark energy and an ultralight massive 3-form, the latter obtained from numerically integrated cosmological histories consistent with $Λ$CDM up to low redshift. Our results show that birefringence from 3-form dark energy can both mimic that from an ALP or be distinguishable, depending on the field configuration in the early universe.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates whether 3-form dark energy can explain cosmic birefringence. The authors consider two EFT-inspired 3-form-photon couplings (dimension-6 gauge-invariant and dimension-4), compute the birefringence angle β, and find that while the dimension-4 operator can accommodate observed β~0.3° (at the cost of exciting the photon's longitudinal mode), the dimension-6 operator requires an extremely large coupling. They derive universal β(z) profiles and compare them to ALP dark energy and ultralight massive 3-form predictions, showing 3-form birefringence can either mimic or be distinguishable from ALPs depending on early-universe field configuration.
AI.motivation: 3-forms are promising cosmological fields capable of explaining inflation and dark energy, with tensorial structure enabling unique couplings not possible for canonical scalars. This work explores whether 3-form dark energy can explain cosmic birefringence, a potential new-physics signal suggested by recent CMB observations.
AI.method: Two EFT-inspired couplings between the 3-form and photon are considered. The birefringence angle β is computed for each operator. The authors derive universal profiles of β as a function of redshift, examining sensitivity to the 3-form potential and initial conditions, and compare with numerically integrated cosmological histories consistent with ΛCDM up to low redshift, as well as with ALP dark energy predictions.
AI.result: The dimension-6 gauge-invariant operator requires an extremely large coupling to explain β~0.3°. The dimension-4 operator can accommodate β~0.3° but excites the photon's longitudinal mode, and a self-consistent decoupling limit implies the photon mass is within a few orders of magnitude of H0. The dimension-4 operator's β is insensitive to the 3-form potential shape but sensitive to initial conditions, while the dimension-6 operator is highly sensitive to the potential shape.
AI.conclusion: 3-form dark energy birefringence can either mimic ALP dark energy signatures or be distinguishable from them, depending on the field configuration in the early universe. This establishes 3-form dark energy as a viable and testable explanation for cosmic birefringence, with different observable signatures depending on the operator and initial conditions.

title: A Gaussian Covariance Matrix for Joint Pre- and Post-Reconstruction Full-Shape Power Spectrum Analysis
comment: 16 pages, 11 figures
summary: We apply the Gaussian covariance formalism to develop a semi-analytical covariance model for the joint analysis of pre-reconstruction, post-reconstruction, and cross full-shape galaxy power spectra. We model the reconstruction-reduced, scale-dependent cross shot noise using displacement-field statistics and introduce a new estimator that directly measures this term. Using the measured power spectra and the modeled shot-noise predictions as inputs, we construct the Gaussian covariance while accounting for correlations between the pre- and post-reconstruction density fields. We validate the resulting semi-analytical Gaussian covariance against mock catalogues. Using emulator-based parameter inference, we demonstrate that the semi-analytical Gaussian covariance adequately captures the dominant contribution to the covariance structure of the full data vector ($P_{\ell}^{\rm pre}, P_{\ell}^{\rm post}, P_{\ell}^{\rm cross}$). For the joint fit to these three power spectra, it yields cosmological constraints consistent with those obtained using the mock-based numerical covariance over the adopted fitting ranges: $k_{\rm max}=0.18\,h\,{\rm Mpc}^{-1}$ for $P_{\rm pre}$ and $P_{\rm post}$, and $k_{\rm max}=0.12\,h\,{\rm Mpc}^{-1}$ for $P_{\rm cross}$.

AI.tldr: The paper develops a semi-analytical Gaussian covariance model for joint analysis of pre-reconstruction, post-reconstruction, and cross galaxy power spectra using the Gaussian covariance formalism, validates it against mock catalogues, and demonstrates that it yields cosmological constraints consistent with mock-based numerical covariance.
AI.motivation: To provide an accurate and computationally efficient covariance model for the joint analysis of pre-, post-reconstruction, and cross power spectra, reducing reliance on expensive mock-based numerical covariances.
AI.method: Applies the Gaussian covariance formalism to model the covariance of pre-reconstruction, post-reconstruction, and cross galaxy power spectra. Models the reconstruction-reduced, scale-dependent cross shot noise using displacement-field statistics and introduces a new estimator to measure this term directly. Uses modeled shot-noise predictions as inputs to construct the Gaussian covariance while accounting for correlations between pre- and post-reconstruction density fields.
AI.result: Validates the semi-analytical Gaussian covariance against mock catalogues. Using emulator-based parameter inference, demonstrates it adequately captures the dominant covariance contribution of the full data vector (P_pre, P_post, P_cross). Joint fits yield cosmological constraints consistent with mock-based numerical covariance for kmax=0.18 h/Mpc (pre and post) and kmax=0.12 h/Mpc (cross).
AI.conclusion: The semi-analytical Gaussian covariance is a valid and adequate replacement for mock-based numerical covariance in joint analyses of pre-, post-reconstruction, and cross power spectra within the adopted fitting ranges.

title: photo-3x2-pt: Cosmology from cosmic shear and galaxy clustering with a single photometric galaxy catalog
comment: 19 pages, 23 figures, submitted to PASJ, comments welcome
summary: We perform a joint cosmological analysis using angular power spectra of galaxy clustering, galaxy-shear cross correlation, and cosmic shear (hereafter referred to as photo-3x2-pt) measured from the Hyper Suprime-Cam year-3 (HSC-Y3) weak lensing shape catalog. We employ the pseudo-$C_\ell$ method to measure these power spectra and use the template deprojection method to mitigate systematics in the galaxy density maps. We perform a standard Bayesian likelihood analysis for cosmological inference based on the measured photo-3x2-pt, including contributions from intrinsic alignments of galaxies, galaxy clustering bias, lensing magnification effect, baryonic feedback effect, and source redshift distribution errors. For a flat cold dark matter model, we find a 68% credible interval of $0.76 \le S_8 \le 0.81$. This result is consistent with those of the HSC-Y3 cosmic shear analyses (Dalal et al. 2023, Li et al. 2023), but is $\sim 25$% tighter than theirs. We also perform a performance test using mock catalogs that mimic the HSC-Y3 data to validate our photo-3x2-pt analysis. Through Bayesian parameter inference of mock data, we verify that unbiased estimates can be obtained for the key cosmological and nuisance parameters, including $S_8$, model parameters of intrinsic alignment, galaxy clustering bias, and shift parameters of the source redshift distributions.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a joint cosmological analysis using photo-3x2-pt angular power spectra (galaxy clustering, galaxy-shear cross-correlation, and cosmic shear) from the Hyper Suprime-Cam year-3 (HSC-Y3) weak lensing data. Using the pseudo-Cl method with template deprojection, they find S8 = 0.76-0.81 (68% CI), consistent with but ~25% tighter than previous HSC-Y3 cosmic shear analyses. Mock catalog tests validate that unbiased parameter estimates can be recovered.
AI.motivation: To extend previous HSC-Y3 cosmic shear analyses by adding galaxy clustering and galaxy-shear cross-correlation information (forming the full 3x2-pt analysis), achieving tighter cosmological constraints, and to validate the analysis pipeline against systematic biases.
AI.method: The authors measure photo-3x2-pt angular power spectra from HSC-Y3 weak lensing data using the pseudo-Cl method, apply template deprojection to mitigate galaxy density map systematics, and perform Bayesian likelihood analysis including intrinsic alignments, galaxy clustering bias, lensing magnification, baryonic feedback, and source redshift distribution errors. They validate the pipeline using mock catalogs mimicking HSC-Y3 data.
AI.result: For a flat cold dark matter model, they obtain 0.76 ≤ S8 ≤ 0.81 at 68% credible interval. This is consistent with prior HSC-Y3 cosmic shear analyses but ~25% tighter. Mock-based inference confirms unbiased estimates for S8, intrinsic alignment parameters, clustering bias, and source redshift shift parameters.
AI.conclusion: The photo-3x2-pt analysis from HSC-Y3 provides improved and consistent S8 constraints compared to cosmic-shear-only analyses, and the validation with mocks demonstrates the robustness of the measurement and inference methodology.

title: Inventories of Rich Carbon-Chain Chemistry in Prestellar and Starless Cores in the Perseus Molecular Cloud
comment: Accepted for publication in MNRAS. 21-page main text (with 12 figures) and 19-page appendix (with 2 figures) for a total of 40 pages
summary: Carbon-chain molecules serve as an important reservoir of reactive organic matter that will eventually be incorporated into protoplanetary disks, planets, and cometary material. Prestellar and starless cores are composed of cold (~ 10 K) and dense (~ 10$^5$ cm$^{-3}$) clumps of gas and dust within molecular clouds, and are nurseries for low-mass stars and planetary systems. Surveys of starless cores have focused on the study of complex organic molecules, COMs, whereas observations of carbon-chains in starless cores are limited. We analyze the carbon-chain inventories of 15 prestellar and starless cores in the Perseus Molecular Cloud. Using Yebes 40m single-dish observations, we detect CS, CCS, CCCS, HC$_3$N, DC$_3$N, and HC$_5$N in at least 10/15 cores and HC$_7$N in 4/15 cores. Our study also finds related isotopologues, where $^{13}$CS, C$^{34}$S, C$^{13}$CS, CC$^{34}$S, H$^{13}$CCCN, HC$^{13}$CCN, HCC$^{13}$CN, HC$^{13}$CCCCN, HCC$^{13}$CCCN, HCCC$^{13}$CCN, HCCCCC$^{15}$N, and DCCCCCN are detected. We report detection statistics, compare column density ratios with Taurus, Serpens, and protostar sources, examine DC$_3$N/HC$_3$N deuterium fractionation, and investigate the relative abundances and correlations between cyanopolyyne (HC$_n$N) and sulfur-bearing (C$_n$S) carbon-chains. The diverse suite of species detected reveals the richness of carbon-chain chemistry in Perseus and illustrates how local environmental conditions, such as density, temperature, and proximity to protostellar activity, shape each core's molecular inventory and relative evolutionary phase. Our findings provide a glimpse into the carbon-chain reservoir of starless and prestellar cores in the Perseus, which may ultimately be inherited by emerging protoplanetary disks and later integrated into planetary systems and biologically relevant material.

AI.tldr: This study presents the carbon-chain molecular inventories of 15 prestellar and starless cores in the Perseus Molecular Cloud using Yebes 40m observations. The authors detect CS, CCS, CCCS, HC3N, DC3N, and HC5N in at least 10/15 cores, HC7N in 4/15 cores, plus multiple isotopologues, and analyze detection statistics, column density ratios, deuterium fractionation, and correlations between cyanopolyynes and sulfur-bearing carbon-chains. The results reveal rich carbon-chain chemistry shaped by local environmental conditions, relevant to material inheritance by protoplanetary disks.
AI.motivation: Carbon-chain molecules are crucial reservoirs of reactive organic matter that feed into protoplanetary disks, planets, and comets. While starless cores are key nurseries for low-mass stars and planetary systems, most surveys have focused on complex organic molecules (COMs), leaving carbon-chain chemistry in starless and prestellar cores understudied.
AI.method: Observational survey using the Yebes 40m single-dish telescope targeting 15 prestellar and starless cores in the Perseus Molecular Cloud. The analysis includes detection statistics for carbon-chain species and their isotopologues, comparison of column density ratios with Taurus, Serpens, and protostar sources, examination of DC3N/HC3N deuterium fractionation, and correlation studies between cyanopolyynes (HCnN) and sulfur-bearing carbon-chains (CnS).
AI.result: Detected CS, CCS, CCCS, HC3N, DC3N, and HC5N in at least 10 of 15 cores, and HC7N in 4 of 15 cores. Detected multiple isotopologues including 13CS, C34S, C13CS, CC34S, H13CCCN, HC13CCN, HCC13CN, and several cyanopolyyne and deuterated analogues. The diverse molecular suite reveals richness of carbon-chain chemistry and shows that local conditions (density, temperature, proximity to protostellar activity) shape each core's inventory and evolutionary phase.
AI.conclusion: Perseus starless and prestellar cores harbor a rich and diverse array of carbon-chain molecules that serve as a reservoir for future protoplanetary disks and planetary systems. The observed chemical diversity reflects local environmental and evolutionary conditions, providing insights into the carbon-chain material that may ultimately be inherited by emerging planetary systems and biologically relevant material.

title: Reanalyzing Megamasers: a low value of $H_0$ from a local probe changes our view of the Hubble Tension
comment: 6 pages, 4 figures, 2 tables
summary: Megamaser distances can be measured without using the traditional distance ladder. As such, they provide an independent probe of the local expansion rate, quantified by the Hubble constant $H_0$. We re-analyze megamaser distance and redshift data to obtain a new, more accurate, estimate of $H_0$. The main improvement in our analysis is the use of a new velocity field reconstruction to correct redshifts for peculiar velocities. This reconstruction utilizes constrained cosmological simulations in addition to redshift survey data to more accurately capture both coherent flows as well as nonGaussian individual galaxy motions. We argue that previous estimates of $H_0$ from megamaser data were susceptible to bias due to peculiar velocities. By correcting for peculiar motions using this new reconstruction we obtain a value of $H_0$ that is consistent with the value from the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) and in tension with the value from the local distance ladder at greater than a $2σ$ level, whereas previous results showed consistency with the distance ladder and tension with the CMB at greater than $2σ$. Our results suggest that the Hubble tension is due to some heretofore undetermined systematic in the distance ladder rather than new physics.

AI.tldr: The paper re-analyzes megamaser distance data to estimate the Hubble constant H0, using a new velocity field reconstruction from constrained cosmological simulations to correct for peculiar velocities. The corrected estimate is consistent with the CMB value and in tension with the local distance ladder at >2σ, reversing previous findings and suggesting the Hubble tension stems from an undetermined systematic in the distance ladder rather than new physics.
AI.motivation: Megamaser distances provide an independent, ladder-free probe of the local expansion rate H0. Previous megamaser-based estimates were potentially biased by peculiar velocity corrections, and the authors aim to obtain a more accurate H0 by improving these corrections, thereby addressing the "Hubble tension" between the local distance ladder and CMB measurements.
AI.method: The authors re-analyze megamaser distance and redshift data with an improved velocity field reconstruction that combines constrained cosmological simulations with redshift survey data. This reconstruction corrects for both coherent flows and non-Gaussian individual galaxy motions, reducing the peculiar-velocity bias that affected prior megamaser H0 estimates.
AI.result: The new analysis yields an H0 value consistent with the CMB measurement and in tension with the local distance ladder at greater than 2σ significance. This reverses earlier megamaser results, which were consistent with the distance ladder and in tension with the CMB.
AI.conclusion: The reversal of the Hubble tension direction implies that the discrepancy is attributable to an as-yet-undetermined systematic error in the distance ladder rather than evidence for new physics beyond the standard cosmological model.

title: Where did all the Little Red Dots go? The abundance of LRD analogues among objects with broad lines at $z < 0.35$
comment: 15 pages, 6 figures. Submitted to A&A
summary: One of the most puzzling discoveries since the launch of the James Webb Space Telescope is a numerous population of sources at high redshift nicknamed ``Little Red Dots'' (LRDs). Characterized by broad Balmer emission lines, compact morphologies and v-shaped spectral energy distributions (SEDs) in the rest-frame optical, the nature of LRDs remains elusive. A major challenge is the high redshift nature of LRDs, which makes observations very expensive and difficult. Finding local LRD analogues is a crucial step in unravelling the physical processes giving rise to LRDs, as cheaper observations with many facilities would become available. In this paper, we conduct a search for local LRD analogues by starting from an unbiased parent catalogue of all SDSS objects with broad H$α$ or H$β$ emission lines (both galaxies and quasars) at $0 < z < 0.35$, complemented by archival photometry and spectroscopy. We find that among broad-line objects, $19\%$ show a v-shaped SED. We then select objects whose SED is well described by a modified black body (MBB), and identify nine local LRD analogues, corresponding to $0.08\%$ of all objects with broad lines. Among only objects which match the typical continuum and emission line luminosities of LRDs, $5\%$ display a v-shape and $0.37\%$ display a MBB-like SED. We recover one previously-identified local LRD analogue (the so-called ``Egg''), validating our methodology. Among the other eight analogues, one (J0302$-$0101) shows all the hallmarks of an LRD despite being visibly embedded in the core of a galaxy; another object is ambiguous, and the remaining six may have alternative explanations for their peculiar SEDs. Our study highlights that LRDs are extremely rare at $z < 0.35$; we find very few objects with broad lines which have LRD-like SEDs, even without attempting to match the compactness of LRDs.

AI.tldr: The authors search for local analogues of "Little Red Dots" (LRDs)—puzzling high-redshift sources from JWST—by screening all SDSS broad-line objects (galaxies and quasars) at 0<z<0.35. They find that 19% of broad-line objects show v-shaped SEDs, and identify nine local LRD analogues (0.08% of broad-line objects), including the previously known "Egg" object which validates their method. Among objects matching LRD luminosities, 5% show v-shapes and 0.37% show modified black body SEDs. Most analogues may have alternative explanations, but one (J0302−0101) displays all hallmarks of an LRD.
AI.motivation: LRDs discovered by JWST are numerous at high redshift but extremely difficult to observe due to their distance. Finding local analogues would enable cheaper, more detailed observations with many facilities, helping to unravel the physical processes behind these enigmatic sources.
AI.method: Starting from an unbiased parent catalogue of all SDSS objects with broad Hα or Hβ emission lines (both galaxies and quasars) at 0<z<0.35, the authors complement this with archival photometry and spectroscopy, screen for v-shaped SEDs, and fit SEDs with a modified black body (MBB) model to identify local LRD analogues.
AI.result: Among broad-line objects, 19% show v-shaped SEDs. Nine local LRD analogues are identified (0.08% of broad-line objects). When restricted to objects matching LRD continuum and line luminosities, 5% show v-shapes and 0.37% show MBB-like SEDs. The method recovers the known "Egg" analogue. One new candidate (J0302−0101) shows all LRD hallmarks despite being embedded in a galaxy core; six others may have alternative explanations.
AI.conclusion: LRDs are extremely rare at z<0.35. Even without matching the compactness criterion, very few broad-line objects with LRD-like SEDs are found locally, underscoring both the uniqueness of LRDs and the value of the few local analogues identified for future detailed study.

title: SPT-3G D1: Foreground-Robust Lensing Templates for Primordial Gravitational Wave Searches
summary: Gravitational lensing of the cosmic microwave background (CMB) generates B-mode polarization that acts as a source of contamination to searches for B modes generated by primordial gravitational waves (PGWs). The strongest constraint on PGW B modes is already significantly limited by lensing B modes, as shown in the most recent BICEP result. In this work, we present CMB lensing B-mode templates constructed using SPT-3G and Planck data, which characterize the lensing B modes and can be used to improve PGW B-mode searches. We use SPT-3G data from the 2019 and 2020 observing seasons for the E modes and the CMB-reconstructed lensing potential, and a cosmic infrared background (CIB) map from Planck as an external lensing tracer. To test for extragalactic foreground biases in the lensing template, we consider CMB lensing reconstruction variants with different levels of foreground immunity: the standard and profile-hardened global minimum variance (GMV) quadratic estimators, and a polarization-only quadratic estimator. We validate the template construction using Gaussian simulations and Agora simulations with realistic non-Gaussian foregrounds. From simulations, we find that foreground-induced biases are strongly suppressed for the template constructed with the profile-hardened GMV + CIB tracer, with residual bias below 10% of the statistical uncertainty on the template power spectrum. Data difference tests on this template similarly show no evidence for significant foreground contamination. This foreground-immune lensing template achieves delensed residual BB power of $A_{\rm lens}^{\rm res} \simeq 0.48$ averaged over $20 \leq \ell \leq 200$, the highest delensing efficiency lensing template to date. These results demonstrate and validate a method to construct foreground-robust lensing templates which will be used in upcoming delensed PGW B-mode analyses of BICEP data.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a CMB lensing B-mode template constructed from SPT-3G (2019-2020) and Planck data, using a combination of CMB-reconstructed lensing potential and external CIB tracers with profile-hardened estimators to suppress foreground biases. The foreground-immune template achieves delensed residual BB power of A_lens^res ≈ 0.48 averaged over 20 ≤ ℓ ≤ 200, the highest delensing efficiency to date, validated through simulations and data difference tests.
AI.motivation: Gravitational lensing of the CMB generates B-mode polarization that contaminates searches for B-modes from primordial gravitational waves (PGWs). As lensing B-modes now significantly limit the strongest PGW B-mode constraints (e.g., BICEP), constructing accurate lensing B-mode templates is essential for delensing and improving PGW searches.
AI.method: The lensing B-mode template is constructed using SPT-3G E-mode data from the 2019 and 2020 observing seasons, the CMB-reconstructed lensing potential, and a Planck cosmic infrared background (CIB) map as an external lensing tracer. To test for extragalactic foreground biases, multiple CMB lensing reconstruction variants are considered: standard and profile-hardened global minimum variance (GMV) quadratic estimators, plus a polarization-only quadratic estimator. The template construction is validated using Gaussian simulations and Agora simulations with realistic non-Gaussian foregrounds.
AI.result: Foreground-induced biases are strongly suppressed for the template constructed with the profile-hardened GMV + CIB tracer, with residual bias remaining below 10% of the statistical uncertainty on the template power spectrum. Data difference tests show no significant foreground contamination. The foreground-immune lensing template achieves delensed residual BB power of A_lens^res ≈ 0.48 averaged over 20 ≤ ℓ ≤ 200, the highest delensing efficiency to date.
AI.conclusion: The results demonstrate and validate a method for constructing foreground-robust lensing templates that will be used in upcoming delensed PGW B-mode analyses of BICEP data, improving the sensitivity of searches for primordial gravitational waves.

title: On the Origin of the Ly$α$ Damping Wing in Galaxies at $8\le z \le 10$: Explorations using the NINJA Simulations
comment: Submitted to Astronomy & Astrophysics (A&A). Comments are welcome
summary: Ly$α$ damping wing measurements of galaxies at $7\leq z\leq14$ with the JWST provide a powerful probe of the Epoch of Reionization. We combine the large-scale cosmological hydrodynamical NINJA simulations with an idealized ionized-bubble model at z=8 and 10 to quantify the contributions of the intergalactic medium (IGM), circumgalactic medium (CGM), and interstellar medium (ISM) to the observed Ly$α$ damping wing. We generate mock Ly$α$ absorption spectra, and consider three idealized scenarios: (i) galaxies embedded in a uniformly ionized IGM, (ii) galaxies surrounded by HII regions with radii of 0-400 pkpc, and (iii) the same models including Ly$α$ absorption from partially ionized gas within the virial radius. We explore IGM neutral fractions ($x_{\rm HI}$) of 0.1, 0.8, and 1.0, and compare the distribution of inferred HI column densities (NHI) with observations to constrain the sizes of HII regions and $x_{\rm HI}$ of the IGM and gas in and around galaxies. Galaxies are surrounded by over-dense gas extending to $\sim$60-100 pkpc, with its extent increasing with halo mass and showing little evolution between z=8 and 10. The inferred NHI also increases with halo and stellar mass. While the observed incidence of damped Ly$α$ absorption and the median NHI can be reproduced by different combinations of $x_{\rm HI}$ of the IGM and HII region size, models with a uniformly ionized IGM or HII regions larger than $\sim50$ pkpc fail to reproduce the strongest absorbers (NHI>$10^{22}cm^{-2}$). Including partially ionized gas within the virial radius substantially increases the incidence of these absorbers, although the predicted values remain below the observations, suggesting an additional contribution from unresolved gas in stellar birth clouds. The strongest damped Ly$α$ absorbers therefore provide a unique probe of the ionization state of the ISM, CGM, and IGM.

AI.tldr: This paper uses JWST Lyα damping wing measurements at z=7-14 to probe the Epoch of Reionization by combining NINJA hydrodynamical simulations with an idealized ionized-bubble model at z=8 and 10. The authors generate mock Lyα absorption spectra under three scenarios (uniformly ionized IGM, HII regions of 0-400 pkpc, and inclusion of partially ionized virial gas) and compare inferred HI column densities with observations. They find that the strongest damped Lyα absorbers (NHI>10^22 cm^-2) cannot be explained by a uniformly ionized IGM or HII regions larger than ~50 pkpc, and that including partially ionized circumgalactic gas increases absorber incidence but still falls short of observations, suggesting additional contributions from unresolved stellar birth clouds.
AI.motivation: To quantify the individual contributions of the IGM, CGM, and ISM to the observed Lyα damping wing at high redshift, and to constrain both the IGM neutral fraction (x_HI) and the sizes of HII regions during the Epoch of Reionization using JWST data.
AI.method: The authors combine large-scale cosmological hydrodynamical NINJA simulations with an idealized ionized-bubble model at z=8 and 10. They generate mock Lyα absorption spectra under three idealized scenarios: (i) galaxies in a uniformly ionized IGM, (ii) galaxies surrounded by HII regions of radii 0-400 pkpc, and (iii) the above models including absorption from partially ionized gas within the virial radius. They explore IGM neutral fractions of 0.1, 0.8, and 1.0 and compare inferred NHI distributions with observations.
AI.result: Galaxies are surrounded by over-dense gas extending to ~60-100 pkpc, with extent increasing with halo mass and little evolution between z=8 and 10. Inferred NHI increases with halo and stellar mass. The observed incidence of damped Lyα absorption and median NHI can be reproduced by various combinations of x_HI and HII region size, but models with a uniformly ionized IGM or HII regions larger than ~50 pkpc fail to reproduce the strongest absorbers (NHI>10^22 cm^-2). Including partially ionized virial gas increases absorber incidence but remains below observations, suggesting an additional contribution from unresolved gas in stellar birth clouds.
AI.conclusion: The strongest damped Lyα absorbers provide a unique and powerful probe of the ionization state of the ISM, CGM, and IGM during the Epoch of Reionization, and highlight the need to account for both circumgalactic and interstellar gas—particularly unresolved stellar birth clouds—in interpreting JWST Lyα damping wing observations.

title: Emission line formation in scattering dominated media: implications for LRDs
comment: main text: 8 pages, 4 figures. appendices: 8 pages, 2 figures. Submitted to ApJ letters
summary: Recent JWST observations of ``Little Red Dots'' (LRDs) reveal broad and prominent Balmer emission lines. We present a theoretical framework for intrinsic emission line formation and broadening within static, optically thick, scattering-dominated gas envelopes with thermal populations. Using random-walk and diffusion approximations, we derive analytical line profiles for lines forming intrinsically within the scattering medium. We demonstrate that a geometrically thin planar photosphere produces a shallow line profile characterized by a logarithmic plateau and a $v^{-1}$ wing. A radially extended photosphere yields a broken power-law spectrum transitioning from $v^{-α}$ to $v^{-(α+1)}$, with $0 < α< 1$. This is in contrast to a scattering medium external to the line-forming region, which produces an exponential line profile. We show that this broken power-law model can fit the $\mathrm{H}α$ line profiles observed in LRDs. Higher quality spectra may be able to distinguish between intrinsic and extrinsic models for the line broadening in LRDs. In our LTE models, the high contrast between the $\mathrm{H}α$ and continuum flux cannot be explained. Quantitative comparison to LRD spectra requires expanding our models to non-LTE situations.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a theoretical framework explaining the broad Balmer emission lines observed in JWST's "Little Red Dots" (LRDs). Using random-walk and diffusion approximations, the authors derive analytic line profiles for intrinsically broadened lines in static, optically thick, scattering-dominated gas envelopes, showing that the LRD Hα profiles follow a broken power-law form distinct from external scattering scenarios, though LTE models cannot explain the observed line-to-continuum contrast.
AI.motivation: JWST observations of Little Red Dots reveal broad, prominent Balmer emission lines, but the physical mechanism producing their broadening remains unclear. The authors aim to provide a theoretical framework to understand intrinsic emission line formation and broadening in the scattering-dominated, optically thick envelopes suggested by LRD observations.
AI.method: The authors develop an analytical model using random-walk and diffusion approximations for line formation inside static, optically thick, scattering-dominated gas envelopes with thermal populations. They derive analytic line profiles for two geometries: a geometrically thin planar photosphere and a radially extended photosphere, and compare these to external scattering scenarios. The resulting broken power-law model is fit to observed LRD Hα lines.
AI.result: A thin planar photosphere yields a shallow line profile with a logarithmic plateau and v^-1 wing. A radially extended photosphere produces a broken power-law spectrum transitioning from v^-α to v^-(α+1) with 0<α<1, which successfully fits observed LRD Hα profiles. External scattering would produce exponential profiles instead. However, LTE models cannot reproduce the high Hα-to-continuum flux contrast observed in LRDs, requiring non-LTE treatment.
AI.conclusion: The broken power-law intrinsic broadening model can reproduce LRD Balmer line profiles, and higher-quality spectra may distinguish intrinsic from extrinsic broadening mechanisms. However, expanding the models to non-LTE conditions is necessary to quantitatively match LRD spectra and explain the observed line-to-continuum contrast.

title: Ruffled Feathers: Merger-driven galaxy size growth and structural transformation in EAGLE
comment: 14 pages, 7 + 7 figures, main results: Figs. 1, 4 and 5
summary: Galaxy mergers drive both the size growth and the transformation from discs to spheroids, yet the prescriptions used to model these processes in semi-analytic frameworks have not been tested against the realistic merger population in cosmological hydrodynamical simulations. Using $\approx 4{,}500$ mergers identified in the EAGLE simulation, we test an energy-conservation estimator for post-merger galaxy sizes and quantify merger-driven morphological transformation. The predicted remnant half-stellar-mass radius matches the simulated descendant size with a scatter of $\approx 0.12$-$0.15$ dex and no significant systematic dependence on progenitor properties, while a commonly used dissipation correction applied to gas-rich mergers under-predicts the post-merger size by up to $\approx 0.4$ dex in a cosmological context and increases the overall scatter. The per-merger size growth increases monotonically with the stellar mass ratio of the merging pair, from $\lesssim 0.03$ dex for minor mergers to $\approx 0.10$ dex for equal-mass mergers. From the energy-conservation estimator, we analytically derive the size growth efficiency per unit accreted stellar mass, $η\equiv \mathrm{d}\log_{10} r_{\star}/\mathrm{d}\log_{10} M_{\star}$, and show that $η$ reaches $\approx 2$ only in the idealised limit of collisionless minor mergers with zero orbital energy; as $η$ is highly sensitive to the orbital energy at the time of merging, the minor merger channel cannot be established as the driver of the rapid size growth of massive galaxies without better constraints on this quantity. Beyond the size growth, mergers systematically reduce rotational support and increase triaxiality in proportion to mass ratio, but even the most nearly equal-mass mergers do not always fully destroy the disc, in tension with the complete disc destruction assumed in several semi-analytic models.

AI.tldr: This study uses ~4,500 mergers from the EAGLE cosmological hydrodynamical simulation to test energy-conservation estimators for post-merger galaxy sizes and quantify merger-driven morphological transformation. The estimator reproduces simulated descendant sizes with ~0.12-0.15 dex scatter, while a commonly used dissipation correction under-predicts sizes by up to ~0.4 dex. Size growth scales with mass ratio (0.03-0.10 dex), and the derived efficiency η reaches ~2 only in idealized collisionless minor mergers. Mergers systematically reduce rotational support and increase triaxiality, but even equal-mass mergers don't always fully destroy discs.
AI.motivation: Semi-analytic models of galaxy formation rely on prescriptions for merger-driven size growth and disc-to-spheroid transformation that have never been validated against realistic merger populations from cosmological hydrodynamical simulations. This work aims to test these prescriptions directly against the EAGLE simulation's merger sample.
AI.method: The authors analyze ~4,500 galaxy mergers identified in the EAGLE simulation. They test an energy-conservation estimator for post-merger galaxy sizes by comparing predicted remnant half-stellar-mass radii against simulated descendants. They also quantify merger-driven morphological transformation (rotational support and triaxiality) and analytically derive the size growth efficiency η from the energy-conservation framework.
AI.result: The energy-conservation estimator predicts descendant sizes with ~0.12-0.15 dex scatter and no significant progenitor-dependent bias, whereas a common dissipation correction under-predicts sizes by up to ~0.4 dex in cosmological contexts. Per-merger size growth ranges from <0.03 dex (minor) to ~0.10 dex (equal-mass) mergers. The derived η approaches ~2 only in the idealized limit of collisionless minor mergers with zero orbital energy. Mergers reduce rotational support and increase triaxiality proportionally to mass ratio, but equal-mass mergers do not always fully destroy discs.
AI.conclusion: The energy-conservation estimator is a valid size-growth prescription for semi-analytic models, while the dissipation correction commonly applied to gas-rich mergers should be reconsidered. The minor merger channel cannot be established as the primary driver of rapid size growth in massive galaxies without better constraints on orbital energy at merging. Semi-analytic models that assume complete disc destruction in mergers are in tension with simulation results.

title: Variations in the 3.3 $μ$m Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbon Feature Across Nearby Galaxies Driven by Metallicity and Radiation Field Spectrum
comment: 39 pages, 24 figures, 3 tables; accepted for publication in ApJ
summary: We use JWST NIRCam imaging to investigate the 3.3 $μ$m polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) feature in nearby galaxies. NIRCam observations of the 3.3 $μ$m feature are emerging as a powerful tool for studying the structure of the interstellar medium (ISM) and the conditions of the dust at ~0".1 resolution. These maps require accurate subtraction of the underlying continuum emission. We present an empirical method to isolate the PAH-correlated emission in the F335M filter using the F300M and F360M filters for continuum subtraction. We find that the slope of the F335M/F300M versus F360M/F300M colors for PAH-correlated emission shows a dependence on local ISM properties, with the strongest dependence on specific star formation rate. Weaker emission features captured by these bands appear suppressed relative to the main 3.3 $μ$m feature in regions of active star formation. We find trends in the 3.3/7.7 and 3.3/11.3 $μ$m ratios that suggest changes in PAH size, charge, and heating by a varying radiation field spectrum. We find decreases in both band ratios with increasing metallicity, which we attribute to a shift to smaller PAH populations at low metallicity. Comparison to optical ionized gas line ratios and dust models show that variations in the interstellar radiation field spectrum influence the PAH feature ratios. This analysis supports inhibited growth formation scenarios for the observed PAH band ratio trends with metallicity and emphasizes the importance of considering the local radiation field characteristics and gas-phase metallicity when using these band ratios as PAH property diagnostics.

AI.tldr: The paper presents an empirical method using JWST NIRCam F335M, F300M, and F360M filters to isolate the 3.3 μm PAH feature from continuum emission in nearby galaxies, revealing that PAH band ratios (3.3/7.7 and 3.3/11.3 μm) depend on local ISM properties, radiation field spectrum, and metallicity, supporting inhibited PAH growth at low metallicity.
AI.motivation: JWST NIRCam observations of the 3.3 μm PAH feature offer a powerful tool for studying ISM structure at ~0.1" resolution, but these maps require accurate continuum subtraction. The authors aim to develop a reliable empirical method to isolate PAH-correlated emission and understand how PAH properties vary with local ISM conditions.
AI.method: The method uses NIRCam imaging in three filters (F335M for the PAH feature, F300M and F360M for continuum subtraction) to empirically isolate PAH-correlated emission. The authors analyze the F335M/F300M vs. F360M/F300M color slope dependence on local ISM properties, measure 3.3/7.7 and 3.3/11.3 μm band ratios as functions of metallicity and radiation field properties, and compare with optical ionized gas line ratios and dust models.
AI.result: The color slope for PAH-correlated emission depends on local ISM properties, most strongly on specific star formation rate. Weaker emission features are suppressed relative to the main 3.3 μm feature in active star-forming regions. Both 3.3/7.7 and 3.3/11.3 μm ratios decrease with increasing metallicity, attributed to smaller PAH populations at low metallicity. Variations in the interstellar radiation field spectrum also influence PAH feature ratios.
AI.conclusion: The analysis supports inhibited growth formation scenarios for PAHs at low metallicity and emphasizes that local radiation field characteristics and gas-phase metallicity must be considered when using PAH band ratios as diagnostics of PAH size, charge, and heating conditions.

title: Investigating radio source population $\&$ spatial characteristics of diffuse Galactic synchrotron emission in the GAMA-23 field with uGMRT Band-3
comment: 16 pages, 9 Figures, 5 Tables, Accepted in The Astronomical Journal for publication
summary: We present uGMRT Band-3 observations of the Galaxy and Mass Assembly (GAMA)-23 field. The observations consist of a total of 33 hours spread over 50 pointings, corresponding to $\sim$ 56 minutes per pointing at the central frequency of 325 MHz. The final image mosaicked from these pointings has a central off-source RMS noise of $109\,μ\mathrm{Jy}/\mathrm{beam}$ and covers an area $65.31\,\text{deg}^2$ with a resolution of $15.8''$. This wide-area deep-field observation provides a radio source catalog of 5741 sources with flux densities ${\geq}\,5σ$. We present complementary uGMRT observations overlapping with the high-frequency ASKAP EMU survey. We derived the spectral index from the matched sources in the GAMA-23 field for the first time. We have studied the statistical properties of diffuse Galactic synchrotron emission (DGSE) in the GAMA-23 field using six different latitude target pointings. We fitted DGSE in the form of power law $C_{\ell} = A(1000/{\ell})^{β}$. Our DGSE amplitude range of $A = 1-20\,{\text{mK}}^2$ and $β$ varies between $1.5-2.4$. This work presents one of the first characterizations of DGSE in the southern sky at 325 MHz, setting a precedent for foreground modeling required for sensitive radio observations with the upcoming SKA.

AI.tldr: This paper presents uGMRT Band-3 observations at 325 MHz of the GAMA-23 field, covering 65.31 deg² and producing a catalog of 5,741 radio sources at ≥5σ significance. The work derives the first spectral indices from matched ASKAP EMU sources and characterizes the diffuse Galactic synchrotron emission (DGSE) using a power-law angular power spectrum, yielding amplitudes A = 1–20 mK² and spectral slopes β = 1.5–2.4. This constitutes one of the first DGSE characterizations in the southern sky at 325 MHz, relevant for foreground modeling for the SKA.
AI.motivation: To obtain deep, wide-field low-frequency radio observations that enable source catalogs, spectral index measurements, and characterization of diffuse Galactic synchrotron emission—critical for foreground modeling in upcoming sensitive radio surveys like the SKA.
AI.method: Using the upgraded GMRT (uGMRT) at 325 MHz, 33 hours of observations were spread over 50 pointings (~56 min each). The final mosaicked image achieved a 109 μJy/beam off-source RMS noise over 65.31 deg² at 15.8″ resolution. A radio source catalog of 5,741 sources above 5σ was constructed, matched with ASKAP EMU data to derive spectral indices, and DGSE was modeled as a power law Cℓ = A(1000/ℓ)^β across six latitude target pointings.
AI.result: Produced a 5,741-source catalog at 325 MHz with 109 μJy/beam sensitivity over 65.31 deg². First spectral indices were derived from matched high-frequency sources. DGSE amplitude A ranged from 1–20 mK² with spectral slope β between 1.5–2.4.
AI.conclusion: This work provides one of the first characterizations of diffuse Galactic synchrotron emission in the southern sky at 325 MHz, setting a precedent for the foreground modeling needed for sensitive SKA-era radio observations.

title: Expanding stellar associations as Galactic accelerometers
comment: 13 pages, 8 figures. Accepted in A&A. Full analysis code is provided
summary: The gravitational potential of the Milky Way is fundamental for understanding the evolution of our Galaxy and the nature of dark matter. We introduce a new method to constrain the Galactic potential using expanding young stellar associations. We exploit the physical constraint that these stars share a common, compact origin to reconstruct their most likely orbits and infer the gravitational potential in which they have evolved. We define the size of an association using the trace and determinant of its position covariance matrix. By integrating synthetic associations backward in different trial potentials, we show how the true potential can be identified as the one that minimises these metrics. We demonstrate that, while current observational errors are still too large, upcoming observations will allow us to distinguish between different potentials. Our results suggest that with Gaia DR4 astrometry and radial velocity errors below 0.2 km/s, the halo mass can be constrained with a precision of 0.6 trillion solar masses and the concentration with a precision of < 0.8 using a single association, albeit with significant degeneracies. In addition, we show that the inferred dynamical traceback age is sensitive to the gravitational potential, suggesting that independent age information can help break existing degeneracies, but also that traceback-age estimates are not independent of the assumed potential. Expanding stellar associations carry information about the gravitational potential in which they have evolved. With the arrival of next-generation astrometry and high-precision radial velocities, they will provide a complementary tool for constraining the Galactic potential.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a new method to constrain the Milky Way's gravitational potential by tracing expanding young stellar associations backward in time. The true potential is identified as the one that minimizes the trace and determinant of the position covariance matrix of the association. Current observational errors are too large, but upcoming Gaia DR4 astrometry and radial velocities (<0.2 km/s) could constrain halo mass to 0.6 trillion solar masses and concentration to <0.8 using a single association, albeit with degeneracies that independent age information could help break.
AI.motivation: The gravitational potential of the Milky Way is essential for understanding Galactic evolution and the nature of dark matter, yet existing methods have limitations. The authors seek a complementary, independent way to constrain the Galactic potential using physically grounded information contained in expanding young stellar associations.
AI.method: The method exploits the physical fact that stars in a young stellar association share a common, compact origin. Synthetic associations are integrated backward in time in different trial gravitational potentials, and the true potential is identified as the one that minimises the trace and determinant of the association's position covariance matrix (defining the association size).
AI.result: Simulations show that while current observational errors are too large, upcoming observations will distinguish between potentials. With Gaia DR4 astrometry and radial velocity errors below 0.2 km/s, a single association can constrain halo mass to 0.6 trillion solar masses and concentration to <0.8, though with significant degeneracies. The dynamical traceback age is also shown to be potential-sensitive, and independent age information can help break degeneracies—but traceback ages are not independent of the assumed potential.
AI.conclusion: Expanding stellar associations carry valuable information about the gravitational potential in which they evolved. With next-generation astrometry and high-precision radial velocities, they will become a complementary tool for constraining the Galactic potential.

title: Cosmological Distance Measurements of High Redshift Blazars: OJ 248 (z=0.939) and 4C +38.41 (z=1.814)
comment: 10 pages, 1 figures, published in JKAS
summary: In this study, we estimated the angular diameter distances to two high-redshift active galactic nuclei (AGNs), OJ 248 (z = 0.939) and 4C +38.41 (z = 1.814), using 43 GHz radio light curves. The aim of this work is to extend AGN variability-based distance measurement methods to the high-redshift regime. The distance estimates were analyzed under two assumptions for the maximum intrinsic brightness temperature TB,int: (1) the equipartition temperature, and (2) the sample-averaged TB,int. As a representative result, when adopting the equipartition temperature, the angular diameter distances to OJ 248 and 4C +38.41 are estimated to be 7592.7 +/- 396.7 Mpc and 11069.8 +/- 1216.9 Mpc, respectively. In addition, Doppler factors were calculated using the inverse-Compton method, and additional distance estimates were obtained based on these values. Our error budget analysis shows that the most significant systematic uncertainty arises from epoch selection. These results indicate that systematic effects have a substantial impact on the derived distance estimates and limit their reliability, particularly in the high-redshift regime. Reducing these uncertainties will require improved observational cadence and reduced post-fit noise. AGN variability provides an alternative approach to distance estimation. However, our results reveal significant limitations in the current methodology and indicate that further methodological and observational improvements are required before its cosmological applicability can be reliably assessed.

AI.tldr: The authors estimate angular diameter distances to two high-redshift AGNs (OJ 248 at z=0.939 and 4C +38.41 at z=1.814) using 43 GHz radio light curves and AGN variability-based distance measurement methods. Distances of ~7593 Mpc and ~11070 Mpc are derived under the equipartition temperature assumption, with Doppler factors calculated via the inverse-Compton method. However, systematic uncertainties—most notably from epoch selection—significantly limit the reliability of these estimates in the high-redshift regime.
AI.motivation: To extend AGN variability-based angular diameter distance measurement methods to the high-redshift regime, providing an alternative cosmic distance estimation approach beyond standard cosmological probes.
AI.method: The study uses 43 GHz radio light curves from two high-redshift AGNs (OJ 248, z=0.939 and 4C +38.41, z=1.814). Angular diameter distances are estimated under two assumptions for the maximum intrinsic brightness temperature: the equipartition temperature and the sample-averaged value. Doppler factors are independently calculated using the inverse-Compton method, and additional distance estimates are derived from these. An error budget analysis quantifies systematic uncertainties.
AI.result: Under the equipartition temperature assumption, angular diameter distances are 7592.7±396.7 Mpc (OJ 248) and 11069.8±1216.9 Mpc (4C +38.41). The error budget analysis identifies epoch selection as the dominant systematic uncertainty source.
AI.conclusion: AGN variability offers a viable alternative approach to distance estimation, but current systematic uncertainties—especially from epoch selection—substantially limit its reliability at high redshifts. Improved observational cadence and reduced post-fit noise are required before the cosmological applicability of this method can be reliably assessed.

title: Scylla: Observational Evidence for an Order of Magnitude in Dust Mass Opacity Evolution with ISM Density in the Large Magellanic Cloud
comment: accepted for publication by ApJ Letters
summary: The emissivity of dust is known to vary greatly with radiative environment, density, grain chemistry, and geometry. Discrepancies between dust mass surface densities derived from far-infrared (FIR) emission and visible extinction persist across and within galaxies in the local Universe. Here, we use new extinction and emission measurements towards the LMC to show that this discrepancy is driven by the dust mass opacity evolving with the intrinsic density of the ISM, and that the ratio between FIR and optical dust mass opacity varies with gas surface density. These new findings imply that the dust mass opacity in the FIR could increase by nearly an order of magnitude (e.g., $κ_{160} = 0.3 - 6\ m^2\ kg^{-2}$) across over an order of magnitude of total hydrogen surface density $(Σ_H = 4 - 100 M_{\odot}\ pc^{-2})$, corroborating previous theoretical models for dust mass opacity evolution in the FIR, and providing new implications for emission-based dust mass estimates.

AI.tldr: This paper uses new extinction and emission measurements toward the Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC) to show that the longstanding discrepancy between dust masses derived from far-infrared (FIR) emission versus visible extinction is driven by the dust mass opacity evolving with the intrinsic density of the interstellar medium (ISM). The ratio between FIR and optical dust mass opacity varies with gas surface density, and the FIR dust mass opacity can increase by nearly an order of magnitude across the range of measured hydrogen surface densities.
AI.motivation: To resolve the persistent discrepancies between dust mass surface densities derived from far-infrared emission and visible extinction, which have been observed across and within galaxies in the local Universe.
AI.method: The authors combine new extinction and emission measurements towards the Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC), comparing FIR emission-derived dust masses with visible extinction-derived dust masses, and analyzing how the opacity ratio varies as a function of gas surface density.
AI.result: The dust mass opacity in the FIR increases by nearly an order of magnitude (κ_160 = 0.3 to 6 m² kg⁻¹) across an order of magnitude of total hydrogen surface density (Σ_H = 4 to 100 M_sun pc⁻²), confirming that the FIR-to-optical dust mass opacity ratio varies with gas surface density.
AI.conclusion: The dust mass opacity in the FIR evolves with ISM density, corroborating previous theoretical models for dust mass opacity evolution and providing new implications for emission-based dust mass estimates.

title: Optical Counterparts of MeerKLASS L-band and UHF-band surveys
comment: 17 pages, 19 figures, submitted to A&A
summary:
Context: Wide-area radio continuum surveys require reliable optical and infrared counterpart identification, but high optical source densities and extended or multi-component radio morphologies make this challenging.
  Aims: We present optical and infrared counterpart catalogs for MeerKLASS L-band and UHF-band on-the-fly continuum sources using KiDS DR5 and DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys DR10 (LS DR10), including counterpart probabilities, redshifts, and host-galaxy properties.
  Methods: We developed the Stellar-mass Enhanced Density Association (SEDA) method, an empirical framework that compares candidate densities around radio positions with those in a position-displaced control catalog. For galaxies we use positional offset, stellar mass, and redshift; quasar candidates are treated separately using offset and mid-infrared selection. A second-pass search associates multi-component radio sources with common hosts.
  Results: In the L-band survey, we identify 20,400 KiDS-based counterparts with $P_{\rm true}>0.5$, corresponding to 66% of L-band sources within the KiDS footprint. In the UHF-band survey, we identify 61,633 LS DR10 counterparts, corresponding to 81% of the radio sources. Spectroscopic redshifts are available for 22% and 44% of the L-band and UHF-band counterparts, respectively. The redshift distributions show low-redshift star-forming galaxies, intermediate-redshift radio galaxies, and a high-redshift tail dominated by quasars. SEDA also recovers rare radio-loud quasars, including QSO J2318-3113 at $z=6.44$ and UHF_DR1 J+111111.8+053626.6 at $z=5.24$.
  Conclusions: SEDA provides a data-driven route to counterpart identification for wide-area radio surveys with complex source morphologies. The catalogs enable future MeerKLASS studies of radio source populations, host-galaxy demographics, and rare high-redshift radio quasars.

AI.tldr: This paper presents optical and infrared counterpart catalogs for MeerKLASS L-band and UHF-band radio continuum sources using KiDS DR5 and DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys DR10. The authors developed the Stellar-mass Enhanced Density Association (SEDA) method, an empirical framework comparing candidate densities around radio positions with a position-displaced control catalog, incorporating positional offset, stellar mass, and redshift for galaxies, with separate treatment of quasar candidates via offset and mid-infrared selection. SEDA identified 20,400 L-band counterparts (66% of sources) and 61,633 UHF-band counterparts (81% of sources), recovering rare high-redshift radio-loud quasars up to z=6.44.
AI.motivation: Wide-area radio continuum surveys require reliable optical and infrared counterpart identification, but high optical source densities and extended or multi-component radio morphologies make this challenging. A robust data-driven method is needed to associate radio sources with their host galaxies.
AI.method: The SEDA method is an empirical framework that compares candidate densities around radio positions with those in a position-displaced control catalog. For galaxies, it uses positional offset, stellar mass, and redshift; quasar candidates are treated separately using offset and mid-infrared selection. A second-pass search associates multi-component radio sources with common hosts.
AI.result: Identified 20,400 KiDS-based L-band counterparts with P_true>0.5 (66% of sources) and 61,633 LS DR10 UHF-band counterparts (81% of sources). Spectroscopic redshifts available for 22% (L-band) and 44% (UHF-band) of counterparts. Redshift distributions reveal low-redshift star-forming galaxies, intermediate-redshift radio galaxies, and a high-redshift quasar-dominated tail. SEDA recovered rare radio-loud quasars including QSO J2318-3113 at z=6.44 and UHF_DR1 J+111111.8+053626.6 at z=5.24.
AI.conclusion: SEDA provides a data-driven route to counterpart identification for wide-area radio surveys with complex source morphologies. The catalogs enable future MeerKLASS studies of radio source populations, host-galaxy demographics, and rare high-redshift radio quasars.

title: The Zero-Age Massive Stellar Population of W49A from VLA Observations
comment: Resubmitted to the AAS Journals following the second referee report
summary: We use all-configuration VLA data at 3.3 cm with a physical resolution of ~2000 AU to infer the embedded zero-age massive stellar population of the W49A protocluster, as traced by its compact, ultracompact (UC), and hypercompact (HC) H II regions. Our method consists of visual source identification, the derivation of stellar ionizing-photon rates from the observed emission measure, and the further derivation of spectral types and stellar masses using state-of-the-art stellar calibrations. Considering the 101 robust detections, maximum-likelihood estimation fitting of the high-mass end (M > 11 M_\odot) of the sample yields power-law slopes Gamma >= 2.56 for the logarithmic representation of the stellar initial mass function (IMF): dN/d(log M) proportional to M^{-Gamma}. The result is robust considering different assumptions for the ionizing stellar systems. The slopes remain at Gamma >= 1.85 after correction for optical depth effects at 3.3 cm. Therefore, the inferred distribution of stellar masses presents a clear deficit in the high-mass end as compared to the standard stellar IMF (Gamma = 1.35). We propose that this is due to a shorter lifetime of the radio-detected H II regions produced by higher-mass stars, but evolutionary effects in the mass distribution of star formation within embedded protoclusters cannot be discarded.

AI.tldr: Using all-configuration VLA 3.3 cm data (~2000 AU resolution), the authors identify 101 compact, ultracompact, and hypercompact H II regions in the W49A protocluster to infer the embedded massive stellar population. Maximum-likelihood fitting of the high-mass end yields IMF power-law slopes Gamma >= 2.56 (>= 1.85 after optical depth corrections), indicating a deficit of high-mass stars compared to the standard IMF (Gamma = 1.35). The authors propose this deficit stems from shorter lifetimes of H II regions around higher-mass stars.
AI.motivation: To constrain the embedded massive stellar population and the shape of the high-mass stellar IMF in protoclusters, which is critical for understanding massive star formation and star cluster assembly.
AI.method: Visual source identification of H II regions in VLA 3.3 cm data; conversion of observed emission measures to stellar ionizing-photon rates; derivation of spectral types and masses using stellar calibrations; maximum-likelihood estimation to fit the high-mass IMF slope and corrections for optical depth effects.
AI.result: 101 robust detections yield power-law IMF slopes Gamma >= 2.56 (M > 11 M_sun), remaining at Gamma >= 1.85 after optical depth corrections. The inferred IMF is steeper than the standard value of 1.35, indicating a clear deficit in the high-mass end.
AI.conclusion: The high-mass IMF slope in the embedded W49A protocluster is much steeper than the standard IMF, likely due to shorter lifetimes of radio-detected H II regions around higher-mass stars, though evolutionary effects in the mass distribution of star formation cannot be excluded.

title: An ALMA study of hub-filament systems II.Quiescent filaments converging towards highly dynamic hubs
comment: 27 pages, 19 figures, submitted to MNRAS
summary: Hub-filament systems are networks of converging interstellar filaments, often with active star formation at their centres, that may play an important role in high-mass star formation. In Anderson et al. (2021) we found that the mass fraction that ends up in a clump's most massive core is significantly higher in IR-dark hubs than IR-bright clumps, suggesting that the most-massive cores form early on. Such early massive core formation requires large inflow rates and dynamically active IR-dark clumps. We now present N$_2$H$^+$(J=1-0) observations of six IR-dark hub-filament systems mapped with ALMA 12m+7m+TP at $\sim 3''$ resolution, to trace the kinematics of the dense gas. The data show intricate emission structures and complex spectra. To characterise their kinematics, we have developed mwydyn, a fully-automated, multiple velocity component, hyperfine line-fitting code. Our results reveal that the emission invariably consists of quiescent individual filaments in the outskirts that converge towards the hub centres where a systematic increase in velocity dispersion and number of components is observed. We also find that the distribution of centroid velocities is remarkably similar between clumps, despite spanning more than one order of magnitude in mass. We propose that our results are best explained by the mixing of gravitationally-driven multi-directional inflows, resulting in highly complex and dynamic hub centres. We also discuss the implications of the observed differentiated filament and hub gas kinematics in the context of the 3D morphology of hub-filament systems.

AI.tldr: This paper presents N2H+(J=1-0) ALMA observations of six IR-dark hub-filament systems, and introduces mwydyn, a fully-automated multi-component hyperfine line-fitting code. The results show quiescent outskirts filaments converging toward dynamic hub centres with increased velocity dispersion and component numbers, supporting gravitationally-driven multi-directional inflow mixing as the explanation for complex hub kinematics.
AI.motivation: Building on previous work (Anderson et al. 2021) showing that IR-dark hubs have higher mass fractions in massive cores (suggesting early massive core formation), this study aims to characterize the dense gas kinematics of hub-filament systems to understand how large inflow rates and dynamically active conditions enable early massive core formation.
AI.method: ALMA 12m+7m+TP observations of N2H+(J=1-0) at ~3 arcsecond resolution were obtained for six IR-dark hub-filament systems. A new fully-automated, multiple velocity component, hyperfine line-fitting code called mwydyn was developed to characterize the complex kinematics revealed by the spectra.
AI.result: The emission consists of quiescent individual filaments in the outskirts converging toward hub centres, where systematic increases in velocity dispersion and number of kinematic components are observed. Centroid velocity distributions are remarkably similar across clumps spanning more than an order of magnitude in mass.
AI.conclusion: The observed kinematics are best explained by the mixing of gravitationally-driven multi-directional inflows creating complex, dynamic hub centres. The differentiated filament vs. hub gas kinematics have implications for understanding the 3D morphology of hub-filament systems and their role in high-mass star formation.

title: Luminosity function of quasars at $1.0<z<3.5$ from SDSS and DESI
comment: 16 pages, 6 figures. Accepted for publication in The Astrophysical Journal
summary: We present a study of the evolution of type 1 quasars at $1.0<z<3.5$, covering the peak epoch of quasar activity. The quasar evolution has been extensively explored by a variety of previous works and the derived quasar luminosity functions (QLFs) are not well consistent with each other, presumably due to the complexities introduced by different quasar selection techniques and associated completeness corrections. We use a new strategy to construct QLFs based on a library of all known quasars. We focus on a wide region of $\sim$1700 deg$^2$ and a deep field of $\sim$265 deg$^2$ that have rich spectroscopic data primarily from SDSS and DESI. We then apply traditional color cuts in the rest-frame UV/optical to select quasar candidates and use the quasar library to identify them. Our final sample consists of 62,426 quasars at $1.0<z<3.5$, with a high completeness ($\sim$96%) and a high purity ($\sim$93%) in the color selection. Simple color cuts can potentially minimize selection biases for the study of quasar evolution. We derive binned QLFs and characterize them using a double power-law model. Sample incompleteness and contamination are considered as part of the uncertainties in the calculation. Compared to previous results, our QLFs are slightly higher at the faint end, and also higher at the bright end at $2.5<z<3.5$. The QLFs suggest that the quasar evolution at $1.0 < z < 2.5$ can be well described by the pure luminosity evolution model, while at $2.5 < z < 3.5$, it can be described by either the pure luminosity evolution or the pure density evolution model.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs quasar luminosity functions (QLFs) at 1.0<z<3.5 using a novel strategy based on a library of all known quasars, applying simple color cuts over large (1700 deg²) and deep (265 deg²) survey regions with SDSS and DESI spectroscopy. The final sample of 62,426 quasars achieves ~96% completeness and ~93% purity. The derived QLFs, fitted with a double power-law model, are higher at the faint end and at the bright end for 2.5<z<3.5 compared to previous results. Quasar evolution at 1.0<z<2.5 is well described by pure luminosity evolution, while at 2.5<z<3.5 either pure luminosity or pure density evolution fits.
AI.motivation: Previous quasar luminosity functions are not mutually consistent due to complexities from different selection techniques and completeness corrections. The authors aim to minimize selection biases by using a color-selection based strategy anchored on a comprehensive quasar library.
AI.method: The authors use a quasar library of all known quasars and apply traditional rest-frame UV/optical color cuts to select quasar candidates in a wide (~1700 deg²) and a deep (~265 deg²) field with rich SDSS and DESI spectroscopic data. Sample incompleteness and contamination are incorporated into uncertainties. Binned QLFs are constructed and fitted with a double power-law model.
AI.result: A final sample of 62,426 quasars at 1.0<z<3.5 with ~96% completeness and ~93% purity. The QLFs are slightly higher at the faint end and higher at the bright end for 2.5<z<3.5 compared to previous work. Evolution at 1.0<z<2.5 follows pure luminosity evolution; at 2.5<z<3.5 both pure luminosity and pure density evolution are acceptable.
AI.conclusion: Simple color cuts based on a complete quasar library can effectively minimize selection biases in constructing QLFs. The results refine our understanding of quasar evolution across the peak epoch of quasar activity, supporting different evolutionary modes at different redshift ranges.

title: Mira variable stars in the galactic bulge and halo
summary: This work aimed to study Miras in the bulge and halo of our galaxy, including those in globular clusters. The AAVSO International Variable Star Index VSX catalogue was used to retrieve Mira variable stars, while the information about globular clusters were taken from the Harris \citep{Harris1976}, McMaster catalogue \citep{33} and Holger Baumgardt \citep{34} table. Stellar characteristics such as metallicity, $T_{\rm eff}$, parallax and colors were obtained by Gaia EDR3 catalogue, Gaia DR3 VariSumarry, Gaia DR3 catalogue, 2MASS Point Source Catalogue, AllWISE, and ZTF catalogue. The UPSILoN program, color-color or color-magnitude diagrams were used to verify that our stars are indeed Miras-type variable stars and whether they are O or C type Miras. To deal with extinction, which affects stars mainly in the galactic bulge, we used IRSA DUST archive, OGLE-III and recalculation to the extiction-free Wesenheit magnitude. We obtained data for 1608 Miras in the bulge, of which 308 are located in 15 globular clusters. For the stars in the halo, we obtained data for 1954 Miras, of which 4 are located in 3 globular clusters. Miras in the bulge show a bimodal metallicity distribution with peaks at \text{--}0.4 dex and $+$0.5 dex, while Miras in the halo show only one peak at $+$0.5 dex. The period of Miras in the bulge is, on average, 30 days longer than for Miras in the halo, and O-type Miras are more abundant in the bulge than C-type Miras. The dependence of the logarithm of the base 10 period on magnitude in the infrared part of the spectrum gives us a linear dependence, with the dependence inverting when a filter is used in the optical part of the spectrum, because of the dust around the Miras.

AI.tldr: This study analyzes 1608 Miras in the Galactic bulge (308 in 15 globular clusters) and 1954 Miras in the halo (4 in 3 globular clusters) using VSX, Gaia, 2MASS, AllWISE, and ZTF data. Bulge Miras show a bimodal metallicity distribution (peaks at -0.4 and +0.5 dex) while halo Miras show a single peak at +0.5 dex. Bulge Miras have periods ~30 days longer than halo Miras, and O-type Miras are more abundant in the bulge. Infrared period-luminosity relations are linear, but invert in optical filters due to circumstellar dust.
AI.motivation: To systematically study Mira variable stars in the bulge and halo of our galaxy, including those residing in globular clusters, in order to understand their stellar characteristics, metallicity distributions, and period-luminosity relations.
AI.method: Data for Miras were retrieved from the VSX catalogue, with globular cluster information from Harris, McMaster, and Baumgardt catalogs. Stellar properties (metallicity, Teff, parallax, colors) were obtained from Gaia EDR3/DR3, 2MASS, AllWISE, and ZTF. The UPSILoN program and color-color/color-magnitude diagrams verified Mira classification and O/C spectral type. Extinction was corrected using IRSA DUST, OGLE-III, and Wesenheit magnitudes.
AI.result: Data for 1608 bulge Miras (308 in 15 globular clusters) and 1954 halo Miras (4 in 3 globular clusters) were obtained. Bulge Miras exhibit bimodal metallicity (peaks at -0.4 and +0.5 dex); halo Miras show one peak at +0.5 dex. Bulge Miras have periods ~30 days longer than halo Miras, with O-type more abundant in the bulge. Infrared logP-magnitude relations are linear, but invert in optical filters due to dust.
AI.conclusion: Mira populations in the bulge and halo differ significantly in metallicity distribution, period, and spectral type abundance. The infrared period-luminosity relation is linear, while optical relations are inverted because of dust surrounding the Miras, highlighting the importance of infrared observations for these variables.

title: Clump Migration in Disk Galaxies: Revisiting Chandrasekhar's Dynamical Friction
comment: 15 pages, 12 figures, Submitted to APJ
summary: Massive stellar clumps are thought to migrate toward galactic centers through dynamical friction, contributing to bulge growth and the structural evolution of disk galaxies. While the classical Chandrasekhar formalism is widely used to estimate clump inspiral times, its validity for extended, evolving clumps embedded in realistic galactic disks remains uncertain. We test this formalism using an isolated disk galaxy simulation by identifying and tracking individual stellar clumps over multiple orbital periods. We develop a position- and mass-based tracking algorithm that follows long-lived clumps and compare their measured orbital evolution with predictions from a dynamical friction model constructed from the simulated baryonic and dark matter mass distributions. After excluding the initial transient phase, we identify nine long-lived clumps, eight of which migrate inward while losing 60-90\% of their initial mass. The analytical model reproduces the overall dependence of migration on clump mass and galactocentric radius, but for six clumps it overestimates the inspiral time by factors of $\sim2$-$10$. Since mass loss would reduce the dynamical friction force, it cannot account for the observed faster migration. Our results suggest that additional physical processes, for example clump-clump interactions, non-circular orbits, and the time-dependent disk potential play an important role in regulating clump migration beyond the assumptions of the classical Chandrasekhar formulation.

Tracking nine long-lived clumps with a position- and mass-based algorithm, the authors find that the analytical model overestimates inspiral times by ~2-10x for six clumps, suggesting that additional processes (clump-clump interactions, non-circular orbits, time-dependent disk potential) beyond the classical formalism regulate clump migration.

AI.method: An isolated disk galaxy simulation is used to identify and track individual stellar clumps over multiple orbital periods via a position- and mass-based tracking algorithm. Measured clump orbital evolution is compared with predictions from a dynamical friction model constructed from the simulated baryonic and dark matter mass distributions.
AI.result: Nine long-lived clumps were identified after excluding the initial transient phase; eight migrated inward while losing 60-90% of their initial mass.
